room: playground, meeting, lunch, arcade, garage, qfn, observatory, spectrum

findings.title: The Meeting power strip can be lost for good in the sealed server closet: no respawn, no reach, no hint
findings.problem:
The Big Meeting server closet is a sealed box. Its walls run x −16.5…−11.775 and z −10…−5.375 with no doorway (src/levels/meeting.ts:35: closet-east and closet-front, plus the back and left shell walls). The walls look 1.35 m high but have a 2.6 m collider (src/levels/decor.ts:44-49). Pip can't hop the collider. A jump-throw (Space, then Q at about 0.36 s) still lobs a held item over it. My script did this from (−13.5, −1.25) facing −z. The required power strip landed at (−14.11, 0.04, −8.27), on the closet floor in front of the racks.

Pip can't get it back:
- Pip can't enter the closet.
- Grabbing needs a horizontal distance under 1.65 m (src/game.ts:192). From every walkable point along the closet walls ((−11.45, −6/−7.5/−9.5) and (−12.5/−14/−15.8, −5.05)), the closest Pip got was 2.84 m. E grabbed nothing, or a nearby box.
- Respawn never fires. The stuck rule only counts an id'd item above y 2.1 m (src/game.ts:341-342), and the out-of-bounds reset only fires below y −3 or outside width/2+1 (src/game.ts:339). The strip sat at y 0.04, inside the bounds, and was still there after 30 s.

The circuit can't close without the placed strip: needsStrip() and stripPlaced() (src/game.ts:246-247) gate leads[0] (src/game.ts:348). The job can't be finished. The only way out is R or Restart, and nothing tells the player that. The card keeps saying 'Fetch the power strip by the printer…'. The objective marker sits over the racks, behind the wall Pip can't pass (stuck-softlock-10). The prompt offers 'Grab the crate' instead. In the survey the strip is invisible behind the closet wall (stuck-softlock-12).

This breaks AGENTS 7 ('stuck items respawn'), DR-15 and DR-25. The throw takes two keys any curious player presses (jump, then throw), next to the job's starting area: the strip starts 5 m from the closet.
evidence: src/game.ts:339 (out-of-bounds reset only below y −3 or past width/2+1)
src/game.ts:246-247,348 (strip required to close the circuit)
mockups/review5/tools/stuck-softlock/meeting.mjs output: 'after10 (-14.11,0.04,-8.27) … closest 2.84 … after 30 s (-14.11,0.04,-8.27) stripPlaced false'
findings.fix:
Two layers. Do both.

(1) Close the hole in the level. Either:
- give the closet a real doorway (for example a 1.2 m gap in closet-front at x −13.2…−12.0, src/levels/meeting.ts:35, which also makes the server room a place Pip can visit); or
- add a fixed lid collider over the closet at y 2.6 (solid(game, 4.73, .1, 4.63, −14.14, 2.65, −7.69) in decor.ts next to line 139), so nothing can be lobbed in.

(2) Replace the height-only stuck rule with a general 'unreachable for 6 s' rule in src/game.ts:341-342.
- At load, build a reachability grid: 0.25 m cells over the floor. Mark a cell walkable when a 0.32 m capsule at y 0.77 doesn't intersect any fixed collider (world.intersectionsWithShape). Flood-fill from level.spawn, through station stands and the lunch door when it is open.
- Each second, for each id'd dynamic prop that is not held, enabled and not Fixed: it is reachable when some flood-filled cell lies within 1.55 m horizontally and |dy| < 1.7. Otherwise increment stuck. Keep y > 2.1 as an extra trigger.
- After 6 counts, respawn it at home. Burst a puff both where it vanished and at home, and play a short pop.

Optional: while an item is pending respawn, pin the objective marker to its home.
findings.verify:
Add tests/softlock.spec.ts, 'meeting: a strip lobbed into the server closet comes back':
1. open(page,'meeting'); walk(-8.6,-3.9,.4); E.
2. walk(-13.5,0.4,.25); walk(-13.5,-1.4,.15); press Space; wait(.36); press KeyQ; wait(1.5).
3. Expect the strip inside x<−11.9, z<−5.5, or the throw blocked by a lid.
4. wait(7). Expect distance(strip, {x:−8.6, z:−3.2}) < 0.5.
5. Then run placeStrip() and switchProjector() from routes.spec.ts, and expect won.

Also add a unit test of the reachability grid: every level's id'd prop homes are reachable, and the closet interior is not. Re-run mockups/review5/tools/stuck-softlock/meeting.mjs. 'after10' should equal the home position. Retake stuck-softlock-10/-12.
findings.verify_reason:
I reproduced this on my first try. I picked up the strip at (-8.6,-3.9) and jump-threw it from (-13.5,-1.25) facing -z. It landed at (-13.19,0.04,-8.40), inside the closet, and was still there 30 s later with stripPlaced false. From the walls Pip got to 1.76 m at best, outside the 1.65 m reach. E grabbed nothing and no prompt showed. In the screenshot the marker cone sits over the racks and the strip is hidden behind them, while the card still says 'Fetch the power strip'. The code matches every citation. meeting.ts:35 has closet-east (z -10..-5.5) and closet-front (x -16.5..-11.775) with no gap. decor.ts:49 makes the collider 2.6 m tall against a 1.35 m visible wall. game.ts:339 resets only below y -3 or outside the room. game.ts:342 counts an item as stuck only above y 2.1. game.ts:192 limits reach to under 1.65 m. game.ts:348 gates the circuit on stripPlaced(). Restart is the only way out, so the job is blocked and P0 stands. | P0 re-check confirmed: I couldn't refute it. The soft-lock reproduces on the first try. I picked up the strip at (-8.6,-3.9) and jump-threw it (Space, then Q 0.36 s later) from (-13.5,-1.25). It landed at (-13.19,0.04,-8.40), inside the sealed server closet. It was still there 10 s and 30 s later, and stripPlaced stayed false.

I tried four ways to get it back. None worked:
- **Reach from outside.** I stood at four points along the closet walls. The closest Pip got to the strip was 1.76 m, at (-11.43,-8.23). Grab reach is under 1.65 m (src/game.ts:192). E grabbed nothing and no prompt appeared.
- **Hopping the wall.** I jumped repeatedly while pressing W, S, A and D against closet-front and closet-east (hop.mjs). Pip's highest point was y 1.92 and Pip never ended up inside. A jump is vertical=7 against gravity 18, about 1.36 m of lift (game.ts:181,320). The wall collider is 2.6 m tall (src/levels/decor.ts:49), and even standing on a desk Pip's feet would only reach about 2.1 m.
- **Respawn.** Stranded props are only sent home when they are above y 2.1 (game.ts:342), or below y -3 or outside the room (game.ts:339). The strip sits at y 0.04 inside the room, so neither fires.
- **Finishing without it.** needsStrip() and stripPlaced() (game.ts:246-247) gate leads[0] (game.ts:348), so the job can't be completed without the strip in place.

The only way out is R, which reloads the page (game.ts:166,178), and nothing tells the player to do that.

The screenshots match:
- In p0check-gap1-stuck-respawn-softlock-01-meeting-strip-after10.jpg the strip is hidden behind the racks and the marker cone sits over them. The card still says 'Fetch the power strip…' and the prompt offers 'Grab the crate'.
- In p0check-gap1-stuck-respawn-softlock-02-meeting-pip-at-closet-wall.jpg Pip is pressed against the wall with no prompt.

The visible wall is only about 1.35 m high and looks easy to throw over. The strip starts about 5 m from the closet, so a curious player can easily cause this. The job can't be finished without a restart, which meets the P0 definition. P0 stands.

The suggested fix works. Adding a lid collider at y≈2.65 alone would close this hole, because a lobbed item would come to rest above 2.1 m and the existing rule would send it home. A general 'unreachable for N s' check is still worth adding as a safety net.

Evidence:
- mockups/review5/tools/p0check-gap1-stuck-respawn-softlock/meeting.mjs: the throw, reach and 30 s respawn checks
- mockups/review5/tools/p0check-gap1-stuck-respawn-softlock/hop.mjs: the wall-hop attempts
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/tools/verify-gap1-stuck-respawn-softlock/meeting.mjs output: 'throw -1.25 -> (-13.19,0.04,-8.40)', 'after10 (-13.19,0.04,-8.40)', best d 1.76 at (-11.43,-8.23), 'after30 (-13.19,0.04,-8.40) stripPlaced false'
mockups/review5/shots/verify-gap1-stuck-respawn-softlock-01-meeting-strip-after10.jpg (strip invisible behind the racks, marker over them, prompt offers 'Grab the crate')
findings.fix_correction: The fix works. A cheaper option for layer (1): the lid collider means anything lobbed over the closet lands on the lid at y≈2.7, where the existing y>2.1 rule (game.ts:342) already sends it home, so layer (1) alone closes this hole. Keep layer (2) as the general safety net. If the full flood-fill grid is too heavy, a simpler version is a per-level list of sealed AABBs (Level.sealed) that the per-second check at game.ts:342 also treats as 'stuck'.

findings.title: The Meeting coupler and the second reel (on its mail cart) can also be lobbed into the sealed closet and lost for good
findings.problem:
The same sealed-closet hole takes the clean route's two parts:
- The coupler, picked at (−3.65, 5.3), landed at (−14.30, 0.09, −8.51). The nearest reachable point was 3.59 m away.
- E at the second reel's spot (−3, 5.3) picked up the mail cart. The selection picked 'mail-cart' over 'extension' (src/game.ts:192-193: both are id'd and get the same −2 bonus). After a second jump-throw the cart ended inside the closet at (−15.80, 0.25, −7.00). The nearest reachable point was 1.98 m away.

Neither respawned after 10 s, because both sit below y 2.1 (src/game.ts:342).

The clean coupler-then-reel route (routes.spec.ts:39-44, the room's intended tidy solution, DR-01) is then impossible. The game gives no hint, and the card's 'coupler first' guidance (objectives.ts:77) now points at an item that is gone. The job can still finish by the coffee-reel or single-reel sprint routes, so this is less severe than losing the strip. But it removes the room's taught solution, which breaks DR-15 and DR-25. The brief asks for any required item that can be lost for good to be filed as P0.

findings.fix: The same closet lid or doorway and the 6-s unreachable rule as the strip finding fix this. Also, in reach() (src/game.ts:193), rank 'extension' and 'coupler' above 'mail-cart' (for example subtract 2.5 for items whose id is in the current step's target set). Then E at the cart takes the reel, not the 8 kg cart, and the cart stops carrying the reel away.

Each must be back within 0.5 m of home after wait(7), and the coupler route from routes.spec.ts:39-44 must then reach won. Also add: standing at (−3, 5.3) with the coupler attached, E gives held==='extension'. Re-run meeting3.mjs.

It ended at (-16.12,0.09,-8.59) inside the closet and was still there after 10 s, hidden behind the racks. The same game.ts:342 gap applies. The priority is wrong, though. findings.title: Lunch: a doorstop thrown into the dark storeroom can't be grabbed, is invisible, and has no prompt. Recovery depends on a hidden cut-and-repair trick
findings.problem:
A jump-throw from the power room (−11, 4.3) facing −z lobs the wedge over the store-front wall into the storeroom, where it lands at (−11.03, 0.26, −2.31).

While the storeroom is dark:
- Nothing inside it can be grabbed: canGrab() returns false for any point in inStore() unless lit() (src/lunch-runtime.ts:143, 145, 172; src/game.ts:192).
- Pip moved the shelf (spec steps), stood 0.95 m from the wedge and pressed E. Nothing happened. The prompt was empty, the wedge was hidden among the dark boxes, and only the marker cone showed where it was (stuck-softlock-21).
- The card keeps saying 'Wedge the kitchen door open with the doorstop'.

Lighting the store needs the kitchen feed powered, and the thick cable runs through the kitchen door. Without the wedge the door shuts as Pip walks to the post and cuts the cable (src/lunch-runtime.ts:224-226, 248). Run output: 'plugged: lit false … dead true'.

The job is recoverable. Standing at the post, F shows 'Repair the burned cable (costs 15)' (stuck-softlock-22). After the repair the door stays shut, the kitchen and store light up, and the wedge can be picked up (stuck-softlock-24).

The problem is that recovery depends on a mechanic the player hasn't been taught, and it costs money. Meanwhile the fridge clock keeps running (the warming bar was orange at 0:57 in stuck-softlock-22). A player who doesn't find the repair is stuck until the fridge spoils. The same lock applies to the mop, bridges, splitters and the baked tray when thrown into the store before the kitchen is powered. This breaks DR-15, DR-25 and DR-37.
evidence: src/lunch-runtime.ts:214,224-226,248 (door shuts and cuts cables unless wedged)
mockups/review5/tools/stuck-softlock/lunch.mjs output: 'dark retrieve ok:false closest 0.95 lit false' then 'repair at post: dead false lit true … cost 60' then 'lit retrieve ok:true'
findings.fix: In LunchRuntime, add a per-second check. If an id'd prop whose home is outside the store (that is, not the capacitor or cooler-box) has sat inStore() while !lit() for 6 s, send it home with the respawn puff. An alternative is to let canGrab() return true for job items within 1 m of Pip in the dark, and draw them with a faint outline glow so they can be found. Also add a lid collider over the store (y 2.6) so it can't be lobbed into, as with the Meeting closet.
findings.verify:
tests/lunch-rules.spec.ts, 'a doorstop lobbed into the dark storeroom comes back':

2. walk(-11,2.5,.25); walk(-11,6.1,.25); walk(-11,4.3,.15); Space; wait(.36); Q.
3. wait(8). Expect the wedge within 0.5 m of (−3, 7), and lunch.lit false.
4. Then run the clean spec from lunch.spec.ts:8 onward to won.

Re-run lunch.mjs. 'after10' should show the home position.
findings.verify_reason: I re-ran the scenario with my own prefix and got the same results. The wedge lobbed from (-11,4.3) landed at (-11.03,0.26,-2.31) in the store, and lit was still false after 10 s. After moving the shelf, Pip stood 0.95 m away, but E could not take it, because canGrab() refuses anything inside the store while it is dark (lunch-runtime.ts:145,172). Running the thick cable unwedged got it cut by the door: 'dead true', with the door angle at 0. findings.title: Respawn feedback is one-sided: items vanish silently from where they were stuck, and falls out of the room respawn with no puff at all
findings.problem:
When the strip was lobbed onto the server racks (y 2.37, stuck-softlock-13), it sat there with the objective marker hidden under the rack top. After 3.5 s it teleported home. The only cue was a 6-particle white puff at home (src/game.ts:342, burst(prop.home…)), which reads well (stuck-softlock-14, -15). Nothing marks the spot it left and there is no sound, so a player looking at the racks sees the strip simply disappear.

Items that leave the room get no cue at all. The arcade tray lobbed over a 2.2 m side cabinet flew over the 1 m right lip collider (src/levels/decor.ts:67-68) into the void, with the marker following it into the void (stuck-softlock-04). The out-of-bounds/fall reset (src/game.ts:339) moves it home with no puff and no sound.

The brief calls for respawn 'with a puff' (DR-15), and the player should understand what happened to the job item (DR-47, AGENTS 2).
evidence: src/levels/decor.ts:67-68 (front and right lips: 1 m colliders)
findings.verify: Retake stuck-softlock-13/-14 with a frame 0.1 s after the respawn: there is a puff at the rack top and at the printer. Retake stuck-softlock-04: the tray returns within 0.5 s of crossing the lip, with a puff at home. Unit test: respawn() emits two bursts.
findings.verify_reason: The code matches. game.ts:339, the fall/out-of-bounds reset, calls only setTranslation and setLinvel: no burst and no audio. game.ts:342 bursts 6 dust particles at prop.home only, with no sound and nothing at the old spot. In the screenshot from the other reviewer (stuck-softlock-04), the arcade tray is floating in the void outside the room with the marker following it. The puff at home is visible in stuck-softlock-14. I did not re-time the arcade fall myself, but the code path is clear.
extra_evidence: src/game.ts:342 (single burst at prop.home, no audio)
mockups/review5/shots/stuck-softlock-04-arcade-tray-on-cabinet.jpg (tray and marker outside the room over the void)
findings.fix_correction: The respawn() helper is right. For the early out-of-room trigger, test against the shell bounds |x|>width/2+0.3 or |z|>depth/2+0.3 and skip the y<1 condition. Above y 1 an item outside the room is already past the lip, and it falls into the void anyway.

findings.title: Interior walls stop thrown props in mid-air 1.25 m above their visible top
findings.problem:
interiorWall() draws a 1.35 m wall but gives it a 2.6 m collider (src/levels/decor.ts:44-49). The comment at decor.ts:20 says this keeps Pip from hopping walls. Thrown props also hit the invisible upper 1.25 m.

Three of my Meeting jump-throws aimed over the closet wall stopped dead in mid-air above the visible cap and dropped straight down to its foot (run output: landed at (−13.27, 0.10, −5.28) and (−12.27, 0.04, −4.92)). In stuck-softlock-09-1 the strip hangs in the air in front of Pip, above the low wall.

The same walls separate Lunch's kitchen, storeroom and lift room (src/levels/lunch.ts:33-39). An object bouncing off thin air reads as a bug. A slightly higher lob still clears the wall into the sealed closet (see the P0 findings), so the invisible extension neither looks right nor seals anything.
findings.fix:
Pick one of these:
- (a) Use collision groups. Put the upper 1.25 m of interior-wall colliders in a group that only collides with the player capsule (Rapier setCollisionGroups, player group 0x0002). Then props fly over freely and Pip still can't hop. Pair this with lids over sealed rooms.
- (b) Make the visible wall match the collider: add a 1.25 m frosted-glass or mesh upper panel on interiorWall, so the room looks enclosed.

Option (b) also tells the player the closet is sealed.
findings.verify: Re-run meeting.mjs with zz −3.6/−3.0. Throws that clear the visible cap must follow a ballistic arc (no y drop at the wall plane). Take a frame at the moment of crossing.
findings.verify_reason: I reproduced it. A standing Q-throw from (-13.5,-4.26) toward the closet stopped at z≈-5.15, the wall plane, at y 1.62–1.76. That is above the 1.35 m visible cap. The strip then slid straight down to (-14.63,0.04,-5.05) at the foot of the wall. In my screenshot the strip hangs above the wall cap in front of the racks. decor.ts:44-49 confirms the visible h=1.35 against a solid collider of 2.6 at y 1.3. A higher jump-throw still clears the wall into the sealed closet (index 0), so the extra height neither looks right nor seals anything.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/tools/verify-gap1-stuck-respawn-softlock/wallhit2.mjs output: frames 0-3 z -5.13…-5.16 at y 1.62→1.76, then falling to (-14.63,0.04,-5.05)
findings.fix_correction: Option (a) makes lobbing into sealed rooms easier, so it must ship together with the lids or doorways (index 0 and index 2). Otherwise it widens the soft-lock. In Rapier, set collision groups on both the upper-wall collider and the player capsule. Props default to 0xFFFF/0xFFFF, so the upper collider needs membership 0x0004 and filter 0x0002, and the player needs a filter that includes 0x0004.

findings.title: There is no soft-lock or respawn spec at all: DR-15 and DR-25 are untested in every room
findings.problem:
grep finds no test that moves a required item somewhere awkward and checks that it comes back. tests/*.spec.ts only cover the clean and chaos routes. The respawn code at src/game.ts:339-342 has no test.

This review found working recoveries:
- Station items (tray, robot, crate, motor cart, pod, mirror) thrown into corners and behind benches were all re-grabbable (station.mjs runs).
- Lunch cut cables are repairable.

It also found the two hard holes above. Without a spec, any layout change (new decor, a new interior wall, clutter seeds) can reopen a sealed pocket, and the regression would show only as a player report. This breaks DR-25's check line ('for each room… P0 if not').
evidence: tests/ (no softlock or respawn spec; checked the routes, lunch, layout and station specs)
mockups/review5/tools/stuck-softlock/station.mjs output (all retrievals ok after pathing around benches)
findings.fix:
Add tests/softlock.spec.ts with three parts:
- (1) A static reachability test per level, using the flood-fill grid proposed in the strip finding through a test-only drive.reach(x,z) helper. Every id'd prop home, station stand, socket target and switchAt must be within 1.55 m of a reachable cell, and no reachable-from-outside pocket may exist that a lob can enter without a lid.
- (2) A drive.place(id,x,y,z) test hook (manual mode only, next to walkTo in src/game.ts:467). For each level and each id'd item, place it in each enclosed or unreachable cell the grid reports, wait(7), and expect it within 0.5 m of home.
- (3) The concrete lobs from the strip and Lunch findings.
findings.verify: npm.cmd test -- softlock passes on all 10 levels. Deliberately deleting the closet lid or doorway must make it fail.
findings.verify_reason: A grep of tests/ for respawn, stuck or home finds only tests/navigation.ts:13, a walk-stall error message. No spec moves an id'd item somewhere awkward and checks that it comes back, and nothing exercises game.ts:339-342. mockups/review5/RULES.md:123 (DR-15) and :171 (DR-25) require exactly this. Missing coverage does not itself block play, so P2 is right. The P0 holes above are the concrete cost.
findings.fix_correction: Keep drive.place() behind the existing ?manual test drive (next to walkTo) so it is not exposed in normal play. The 'no reachable-from-outside pocket without a lid' check needs the lid and sealed data in the level definitions, so it can't be derived from the grid alone. Add Level.sealed AABBs, or test lob trajectories explicitly.

notes.playability:
I tested DR-15 and DR-25 on real builds with mockups/review5/tools/stuck-softlock/*.mjs. g.close() returned [] every time, so there were no console errors (DR-80 ok).

What works:
- **Station rooms.** The arcade tray, garage robot, QFN parts crate, observatory motor cart, spectrum pod and spectrum mirror were thrown into corners, behind shelves and over or behind benches. After advance(10) each one could be walked to and picked up with E, usually from 0.3–0.7 m. Pip pushes dynamic props (setApplyImpulsesToDynamicBodies), and the 1.65 m reach goes through clutter, so floor-level wedges behind furniture were never fatal.
- **High respawn.** It works: the Meeting strip on the 2.3 m racks went home after 3.5 s with a clear white puff.
- **Out of the room.** Items lobbed over the 1 m front or right lips fall into the void and come back through the y<−3 rule.
- **Lunch cut cables.** They show a red bolt badge and 'F Repair the burned cable (costs 15)', which can be repeated, so DR-25's 'cut part is recoverable' holds in Lunch.
- **Cable chaos.** Playground and Meeting cables can't be cut. Sprint-overstretching and letting go (Q) leaves the plug at Pip's feet, F re-grabs it, and both jobs were finished afterwards (Playground won at 22 s by the clean route, Meeting at 40 s by the coffee reel). There are no doors on those floors.

What fails:
- **Sealed pockets.** The real hole is not 'behind furniture' but sealed pockets you can lob into: the Meeting server closet (strip, coupler, reel cart lost for good) and Lunch's dark storeroom (items can't be grabbed until the kitchen is powered).
- **Controls note.** The brief and DR-22 say Space throws. In the build Space jumps and Q throws or lets go (src/game.ts:166, 183). The rulebook line should be corrected.
notes.clarity:
When a job item is stranded, nothing tells the player:
- The card keeps its text and the prompt offers nearby junk ('Grab the crate', 'Grab the chair').
- The objective marker follows the item behind walls (into the closet) or into the void beyond the arcade's right lip.
- In the dark Lunch storeroom the item itself is invisible among the boxes, with only the marker cone showing where it is.

The respawn puff at home reads well, but there is no cue where the item vanished.
notes.fun: Lobbing items with a jump-throw is fun and physical, and it is exactly what a Good Job player does first. That is why the sealed closet matters: the most natural experiment in the Meeting's opening area, 5 m from the strip, ends the run silently. Once the pockets are sealed or covered by a general unreachable rule, throwing stays a safe toy.
notes.teaching: Out of scope for this gap-fill. One note: in Lunch, the recovery path (let the door cut the cable, then repair it at the post) teaches 'doors cut cables' by accident. A respawn for items thrown into the dark store would keep the lesson on wedging the door instead of on a costly repair loop.
notes.models: Out of scope. One observation: interior walls show 1.35 m but collide at 2.6 m, so thrown props stop in mid-air above the visible cap (stuck-softlock-09-1).

rechecked: M10 (strip snaps within 2.6 m of the door): still fixed. stripPlaced is true after an E-drop at (11.2, −1.4) (meeting2.mjs).
LR16 (the door cuts a cable when not wedged): intended and confirmed. The cut is recoverable with the 'Repair the burned cable (costs 15)' prompt (stuck-softlock-22).
LR6 (a cut cable no longer shows the gold meter): still fixed. The cut thick cable draws black with a red bolt badge, and lit stays false until repaired (stuck-softlock-22).
M2 (props sinking into decor stacks): not re-tested directly. The closet tests show decor.ts colliders are present for the racks (solid 4×2.3×0.9) and the strip rests on top of them, then respawns.

DR-15 'Known' (respawn only above y 2.1, below y −3 or out of bounds): confirmed in the code. In practice, floor-level wedges behind furniture were all recoverable thanks to the 1.65 m reach. The real P0 holes are sealed pockets (the Meeting closet) and the dark Lunch storeroom.
DR-80 (zero console or page errors, browsers closed): every stuck-softlock script returned errors [] from g.close().
